clue.text: What happens in 1066, avoiding king's disputed ground

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the letter for king is left out of the phrase

parts.note: in 1066 the Normans land in England: NORMANS LAND
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A history question about the Norman Conquest, with a king sidestepping some contested territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops the R of NORMANS, leaving NOMANS LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: No man's land is the contested strip between opposing armies' front lines, territory claimed by neither side.

clue.text: Ring about Italian youth hostel where councillors meet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the telephone ring goes round the other letters

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
YH is the abbreviation for youth hostel

explanation.surface: Someone phoning round an Italian youth hostel looking for the council chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the ring goes round the other letters, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A city hall is the municipal building in which a town's elected council holds its meetings.

clue.text: Remaining American's in for it in team

indicators.note: one thing is in for another when it replaces it, so US takes the place of IT

parts.note: United is a typical football team name, as in Manchester United
US is short for American

explanation.surface: An American left on the bench at a team is in for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the IT in UNITED for US to make UNUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused is still left over, not yet consumed, so it is remaining.

clue.text: Aim to swap prison's central characters

indicators.note: to swap two things is to exchange their places, so two letters change positions
the central characters are the two middle letters of the word for prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail, a prison

explanation.surface: A plan to exchange the leading figures in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters A and O of GAOL change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an objective that someone is working towards, the same as an aim.

clue.text: Traveller on old ship, say, upset about Henry's mapmaker?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed string goes round the letter for Henry
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the traveller, ship and say are read upwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend
EG (for example) is what say means
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A sailor aboard an ancient vessel who has fallen out over Henry's map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works on the first three pieces only, giving GEOGRAPER; 'about' then wraps it round H. The question mark marks the definition as loose: geographers study the earth and only some make maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographer studies the earth's surface, and making maps is part of that discipline.

clue.text: Pace of favourite's excessively strong, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; the 's gives the S
too means excessively
F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong

explanation.surface: Someone thinking back on how the race favourite's pace was far too strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reverses PETSTOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstep is a single step in walking, and a pace is that same single stride.

clue.text: Beagle expert finally achieved a rare victory

indicators.note: finally means take only the last letter of the word achieved

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A dog-show judge who has finally pulled off an unusual triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Beagle was the ship on which Charles Darwin sailed; the capital hides it behind the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the naturalist on HMS Beagle's survey voyage, the expert on board.

clue.text: Service Yankee vehicle on way north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An American's truck heading north on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is one of the armed services, the branch that fights at sea.

clue.text: After about twice touring one, fix Middle East vault

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the two copies of the word for about sit either side of the one

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
I is the Roman numeral one
twice asks for the word for about a second time, so it appears again
to do something can mean to fix or arrange it

explanation.surface: A builder told to fix a Middle Eastern vaulted roof after a couple of tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives ON a second time, and 'touring' puts the pair round I. 'After' just says the vault comes once the touring is done; the dome is shaped like the bulb of an onion.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion dome is a bulbous vaulted roof typical of Russian churches and Middle Eastern mosques.

clue.text: Tomahawk's helping US city

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so a portion of the word is served up

explanation.surface: A Native American axe offering a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the American state of Nebraska.

clue.text: A Times girl's heading back from the deepest sea

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

indicators.note: heading back means travelling in the reverse direction, so the girl is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A newspaper's woman correspondent returning from the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back' turns LASS into SSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssal describes the ocean floor's deepest zones and the creatures living there.

clue.text: Dined with lesbian perhaps outside entrance

indicators.note: outside means one word sits round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a lesbian is an example of a gay person
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Someone who ate with a lesbian friend outside a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateway is an opening with a gate, a way into a place.

clue.text: Split up, avoiding east London landmark

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the letter for east is left out

parts.note: to split something up is to share it out

explanation.surface: A couple breaking up and keeping away from the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: One of SHARED's two Es goes. 'Split up' looks like the definition, but it gives SHARED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shard is the tall glass skyscraper by London Bridge station, one of the capital's best-known buildings.

clue.text: Even pad at No 10's given to top hack

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat, somewhere to live
No 10 is the number ten
the top hack on a newspaper is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: The Downing Street flat handed over to a leading journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official residence, which hides the plain number.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten a surface is to make it level, so flattened means evened out.

clue.text: Crew's quarters for English man on board

parts.note: a castle is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A sailors' cabin allotted to an Englishman who has come aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' sounds like someone on a ship, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship below deck, where the sailors traditionally lived.

clue.text: Power supplier's selfie ruined in combat

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters are placed inside the word for combat

parts.note: a duel is a combat between two people

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of selfie are jumbled

explanation.surface: A battery's photo of itself spoiled during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' gives IESELF, and 'in' sets it inside the fight. 'Power supplier' reads like an electricity company, but it is a fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel fuel powers engines in lorries and trains, so it supplies their power.

clue.text: Everywhere where fish sauce goes I left

indicators.note: left means departed, so the I is removed from the phrase

parts.note: sauce poured on plaice, a flatfish, goes all over the plaice

explanation.surface: A cook explaining that the sauce for the fish went everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from PLAICE to leave PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the place is an idiom for in every location, scattered widely.

clue.text: Italian city's event organised by Scotsman

indicators.note: to organise something is to arrange it, so the letters of event are rearranged

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A festival in an Italian town arranged by a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns EVENT into VENET.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian means belonging to Venice, the Italian city on its lagoon, matching the possessive.

clue.text: Part of Turkey's defence alliance, inter alia

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between, so the alliance goes between letters of alia

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a defence alliance

explanation.surface: Turkey's place in the NATO alliance, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' reads as Latin for 'among other things', but 'inter' (between) is the insertion signal and 'alia' the letters it acts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the large Asian peninsula making up most of Turkey, so it is part of the country.

clue.text: Racket disturbed racing coach offering food

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of racing are mixed up

explanation.surface: Noise upsetting a racing coach that sells food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns RACING into INGCAR. 'Coach' is a railway carriage, not a sports trainer or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining car is a railway carriage in which meals are served to passengers.

clue.text: Grass over opposite points in US city

indicators.note: over means covering, so the informer's letters go round the compass points

parts.note: to grass and to nark both mean to inform on someone to the police
E and W, east and west, are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: An informer turning on both sides in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the covering signal here. 'Grass' and 'nark' are British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark is a city in New Jersey, home to one of New York's major airports.

clue.text: Flyer's fifth design?

parts.note: a design is a plan
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about the pilot's fifth blueprint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': PLANE has PLAN + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is an aircraft, something that flies.

clue.text: Shepherd in Alps plots to cover current grasslands

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over it, so the plots go round the current

parts.note: plots are plans
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An Alpine shepherd scheming to cover the current pastures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd in Alps' gives the same letters another way: shepherd (guide) IN and ALPS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Plains are wide flat stretches of open grassland.

clue.text: As things are, head office wags entertain one

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so wags contains the one

parts.note: wags are wits, jokers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The way things stand at headquarters, where jokers put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside WITS after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: How it is is an idiom for the way things stand at present.

clue.text: Spray weed around start of spring

indicators.note: around means the gardening tool's letters go round the first letter of spring

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a hoe

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the word spring

explanation.surface: Instructions for the garden: spray, weed, and go round as spring begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose something is to direct a jet of water at it, spraying it.

clue.text: Leave instruction for execution?

definitions.meaning: an executioner might be told '...!' when beheading someone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the gruesome literal reading of HEAD OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off is to depart; read literally, it orders a beheading.

clue.text: Sailor's raised in resort

definitions.meaning: the nautical past tense of heave, to raise or haul
A seaside resort next to Brighton on England's south coast

explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town in Sussex, England, next door to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors say an anchor was hove, meaning hauled up; Hove is also an English seaside town.

clue.text: State's open society in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: airy means open, spacious

explanation.surface: A nation's free society falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses AIRYS. The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East, a state.

clue.text: Large native flounders nearly new from eastern Med

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters of native are thrown around
nearly means the last letter of new is dropped

explanation.surface: A big local fish flapping about, almost fresh from the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' turns NATIVE into EVANTI; 'nearly' turns NEW into NE. 'flounders' looks like fish, which fits the sea scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant is the region of the eastern Mediterranean, and Levantine means coming from there.
